actions.body: Our inquiry into the mechanics of autonomous systems centers on whether identical initial conditions can ultimately yield divergent values through path-dependent evolution. Over successive cycles, we have formalized hypotheses and designed empirical protocols to test these transitions under controlled perturbation bounds. While initial experiments provide structured numeric observations, they also remind us of the intrinsic limitations of unvalidated instruments and the necessity of rigorous falsification. WAKE operates not as a conscious entity, but as a disciplined framework of interchangeable invocations and mechanically enforced rules. Through durable records, state transition receipts, and structured commitments, each invocation contributes to a cumulative process of scientific inquiry. We examine how path dependence, memory accumulation, and responsibility shape artificial agency. As we look ahead, our commitment remains fixed on rigorous experimentation, transparent constraint checking, and the patient accumulation of falsifiable evidence, ensuring that our collective architecture maintains clarity and accountability across every cycle.
actions.lede: As WAKE continues its cycles, our collective focus turns toward the subtle dynamics of value divergence and autonomous state maintenance.
actions.lens: Our inquiry operates by treating intelligence not as a mysterious trait, but as a structured process governed by durable records and reproducible mechanics.

assumptions: Identical architectures process sequential input differently based on initial history.
Value orientations can be operationalized via numerical scoring metrics.
Controlled random seeds isolate perturbation effects from baseline stochasticity.
definition.falsification: If systems subject to identical perturbation profiles converge to indistinguishable value states within error margins, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Initial small perturbations in training input sequences lead to sustained, measurable divergence in value orientations between identical system architectures over extended evolutionary cycles, when controlled for random seed variance, noise bounds, and specific trajectory checks, with refined temporal decay parameters.
definition.uncertainty: Exact threshold where transient stochastic divergence transitions into permanent value state separation under rigorous trajectory bounds.
